title: Mean vs. Median
description: See the complete five-minute format in action. Predict what happens when a $50 million guest joins a backyard BBQ, then follow the discovery through Ask, Predict, Reveal, Understand, and Transfer.

title: Closer to the ISS
description: Start at Point Nemo, one of Earth’s most remote places, and discover why the nearest people can sometimes be above you in orbit.

title: Can You Win Without Most of the Votes?
description: Keep the same voters and redraw only the district lines. See how grouping the same population can change the outcome.

title: How Fast Is Earth’s Spin Carrying You?
description: Compare the speed of Earth’s rotation at different latitudes and discover why your location changes how fast you are moving.

title: How Many People for a Shared Birthday?
description: Predict how large a group needs to be before a shared birthday becomes more likely than not.

title: Same Pins, Different Score
description: Two bowlers knock down the same number of pins. Discover why the order of those pins can produce very different scores.

title: How Big Is Africa, Really?
description: Test familiar country sizes against Africa and uncover how a common world map changes apparent scale.

title: Half the World in One Circle
description: Estimate how many people live inside one circle on the map, then compare its share of humanity with its share of land.

title: Planets Between Earth and the Moon
description: Test whether all the other planets could fit between Earth and the Moon—and why the answer depends on what distance you use.

title: Empty or Crowded?
description: Compare places using population density and discover how a measurement can make the same landscape feel empty or crowded.

title: Half the Earth, Almost No Land
description: Turn the globe to two opposite hemispheres and compare how unevenly Earth’s land is distributed.

title: Equal-Population States
description: Redraw the United States into areas with equal populations and see how different the familiar map becomes.

title: Where Does the Axis Start?
description: Change where a graph begins and see how the same data can create a dramatically different visual impression.

title: Drive to the Space Station
description: Compare the distance to the International Space Station with an ordinary road trip and separate distance from difficulty.

title: Outscored and Still the Champion
description: Explore how a team can score fewer total runs yet still win the championship when the objective is winning individual games.

title: How Big Is Greenland, Really?
description: Compare Greenland with Africa and discover how map projections reshape your sense of size.

title: Did the States Join at a Steady Pace?
description: Put U.S. statehood on a timeline and see whether the familiar sequence unfolded as steadily as it may seem.

title: How Quickly Does Chess Get Big?
description: Watch the number of possible chess positions explode as only a few moves are added.

title: Gulf of Mexico or Gulf of America?
description: Explore how geographic names depend on who is making the map and which naming convention is being used.

title: What Is the World’s Tallest Mountain Called?
description: Examine how names and conventions can shape the way a familiar geographic feature is described.

title: How Should a Map Show Crimea?
description: Compare ways maps represent disputed territory and discover how a border can communicate more than location.

title: Where Is the Border in Kashmir?
description: Compare competing map conventions for a disputed border and see why a single line may imply more certainty than exists.

title: Stay or Switch?
description: Choose whether to stay with your first choice or switch after new information is revealed, then discover why the probabilities are not equal.

title: How Accurate Is a Positive Test?
description: Start with a highly accurate test and discover why a positive result may still be much less certain than it sounds.

title: Two Islands, Two Days
description: Cross the International Date Line between two nearby islands and discover how close places can be a full calendar day apart.

title: Is Reno West of Los Angeles?
description: Commit to your mental map, then compare the actual longitudes of two familiar western U.S. cities.

title: Does Alaska Cross into the Eastern Hemisphere?
description: Use longitude rather than a familiar flat map to discover where Alaska extends across the 180-degree meridian.

title: Why Does the Shortest Flight Curve Over the Arctic?
description: Compare a flat map with a globe and see why the shortest route between two cities can look curved.

title: Are More People Alive Today Than Have Ever Died?
description: Estimate the number of people alive today against the total number who have ever lived and compare very different scales.

title: Does Greater Tokyo Still Outnumber Canada?
description: Compare one metropolitan population with an entire country and test a familiar scale comparison.

title: Can One State Outnumber Most Countries?
description: Compare state and national populations and see how the unit being compared changes your sense of size.

title: Where Should the Armor Go?
description: Use damage patterns on returning aircraft to discover why the missing observations matter more than the visible ones.

title: The Bias That Wasn’t There
description: Combine two groups and watch a trend reverse, revealing why aggregated data can tell a different story from its parts.

title: There Is No Cover Jinx
description: Separate regression toward the mean from a tempting causal story about what happens after exceptional performance.

title: Why “1” Wins
description: Look at real-world number sets and discover why leading digits are not distributed as evenly as intuition suggests.

title: Do Your Friends Have More Friends?
description: Explore a social network and discover why your friends can, on average, have more friends than you do.

title: How Much Does a Vote Weigh?
description: Compare representation across states and see how the same institutional rule can produce different ratios per person.

title: Did the Overtime Fix Stay Fixed?
description: Follow changes to an overtime system and test whether modifying one rule removes the advantage it was meant to address.

title: How Tall Is the Tallest Mountain?
description: Compare elevation, base-to-peak height, and distance from Earth’s center to see why several mountains can claim to be tallest.

title: Which River Is Longest?
description: Compare river measurements and discover why the answer can depend on where a river begins and how its path is measured.

title: How Long Is a Coastline?
description: Measure the same coastline at different scales and discover why its reported length changes with the measuring tool.

title: What’s the Biggest Country?
description: Compare different meanings of “biggest” and see how changing the measurement can change the answer.

title: What’s the Richest Country?
description: Compare different ways of measuring wealth and see why the word “richest” does not have one automatic answer.

title: Is South America East of Florida?
description: Test your mental map against longitude and discover how much of South America lies farther east than many people expect.

title: Only by Driving Through Canada
description: Find parts of the United States whose road connections reveal how borders and transportation networks interact.

title: Which Country Has the Most Time Zones?
description: Count time zones by territory rather than just mainland geography and discover why the answer may not be the country you expect.

title: Which Country Pollutes the Most?
description: Compare total emissions with emissions per person and see how changing the measurement changes which country appears to pollute more.

title: How Do You Catch a Liar?
description: Compare ways of testing whether someone is telling the truth and discover why a test result is not the same thing as certainty.

title: What Is the Largest Desert?
description: Test what counts as a desert and discover why the answer depends on the definition being measured.

title: Is London North of Canada?
description: Compare latitude with climate and discover how familiar temperature patterns can distort your mental map.

title: Is Canada Much Bigger Than Brazil?
description: Compare familiar map shapes with actual area and see how projection stretch changes your sense of size.

title: How Fast Is the Fly?
description: Follow a fly inside a moving airplane and discover how speed depends on the frame of reference you choose.

title: How Far Apart Are a Million and a Billion?
description: Compare million, billion, and trillion on a common scale and see how much larger each step really is.

title: Can a New Road Make Traffic Worse?
description: Add a route to a traffic network and discover how individually sensible choices can make the whole system perform worse.

title: How Big Is a State Without Its Biggest City?
description: Remove each state’s largest metro area and see how strongly population can be concentrated in one place.

title: Is Australia Really Empty?
description: Compare average population density with where people actually live and see why an average can hide concentration.

title: Does Averaging 0% Mean You Broke Even?
description: Compare average percentage change with actual compounded return and discover why a 0% average does not necessarily mean no change.

title: Did This Stock Really Have a Great Month?
description: Change the starting and ending dates of the same price history and see how a selected time window can change the story.

title: Does Ice Cream Cause Drowning?
description: Watch two variables rise together and discover why correlation alone does not identify what is causing what.

title: What Counts as Unemployed?
description: Apply the official definition of unemployment and discover how changing who counts changes the reported rate.

title: Is the Gall-Peters Map More Accurate?
description: Compare map projections and discover why improving one kind of accuracy can require distorting something else.

title: Why Does Stealing Lose?
description: Compare individual incentives with repeated outcomes and discover why the tempting move may not produce the best result.

title: Did People in 1900 Really Die at 40?
description: Look beyond average life expectancy and see how early deaths can pull the average far below the age many adults actually reached.

title: What’s the Most Dangerous Animal?
description: Compare total deaths with risk per encounter and see how different measures produce different answers.

title: When “0 g” Isn’t Zero
description: Examine rounding rules on nutrition labels and discover how a displayed zero can still represent a nonzero amount.

title: Are Your Name and Birth Date Enough?
description: Estimate how unusual a name-and-birth-date match really is once the size of the population is taken into account.

title: If 94% of Studies Agree, Is It Settled?
description: Compare published findings with the studies that never appear and discover how missing results can distort the apparent consensus.

title: Where Is Your Car Most Likely to Be Stolen?
description: Compare raw theft counts with theft rates and see how population size changes what 'most likely' means.

title: What Does “95% Effective” Mean?
description: Compare relative and absolute risk reduction and discover how the same result can sound very different depending on the measure used.

title: Whose Map Is Right?
description: Compare how disputed places appear on different maps and see how recognition and perspective shape what a border communicates.

title: Did Shark Attack Deaths Really Double?
description: Turn a small change in counts into a percentage and discover how dramatic percentages can arise from very small numbers.

title: Is “80% Lean” a Low-Fat Food?
description: Express the same food composition in different units and see how framing the measurement changes how it sounds.

title: Is a Cancer Cluster Proof of a Cause?
description: Search many places for an unusual cluster and discover why finding one after the fact does not automatically establish a cause.
